text:
Maya: heads-up — saw a p95 regression in eu-west for the new v2-quant model after yesterday's routing tweak. anyone else?
Devon: saw it too, p50 mostly fine but p95 spiked ~220ms -> ~380ms on small requests. looks regional.
Sasha: pinging @Ryan and @Lei — we changed edge routing policy from nearest-pop to cost-priority for a subset of traffic at 02:15 UTC. could be cross-pop hops.
Ryan: confirmed, policy change rolled at 02:12. rule applied to model tag `v2-quant` to prefer cheaper instances in us-east.
Lei: quick note — eu-west capacity is H100-spot pool, cold-backing to us-east A100s when local throttle hits. that would add RTT and kernel warmup.
Maya: ok can we get p50/p95 numbers per region (us-east / us-west / eu-west) before/after? PerfBot: generating summary...
PerfBot: ```
summary: v2-quant small-ctx (gen=64, batch=1)
before (01:45-02:10 UTC): us-east p50 48ms p95 90ms | us-west p50 60ms p95 110ms | eu-west p50 55ms p95 95ms
after  (02:20-02:50 UTC):  us-east p50 50ms p95 95ms | us-west p50 62ms p95 115ms | eu-west p50 58ms p95 380ms
notes: eu-west tail increased, correlation with cross-pop routing and kernel mismatch.
```
Devon: looks like eu-west requests were routed to us-east in many cases — packet trace shows ~70% egress for that tag.
Sasha: do we have kernel mismatch events? e.g., some pods on eu-west were running int8 kernels, fallback to f16 on us-east?
Lei: checked infra logs: ~30% of us-east replicas use f32-optimized kernel due to model conversion in progress. when eu-west routed to us-east, they hit f32 path then fallback to slower path (KV cache misses).
Maya: so two factors: network RTT + slower kernel path. can we reproduce with a small bench?
Ryan: i'll run a targeted benchmark: 1000 single-token requests from eu-west edge with controlled routing (nearest vs cost-priority) and record p50/p95, also test kernel variants (int8 vs f32).
Devon: while Ryan runs that, quick ask — any recent quantization changes to v2-quant? build 2026-03-15 rolled minor scale tweak.
Sasha: quant config unchanged. but conversion pipeline has a pending job that replaced some int8 kernels with a new fused-attn kernel on us-east only.
PerfBot: benchmark job queued: bench-178980-1 (eu-west->nearest), bench-178980-2 (eu-west->cost-priority), bench-178980-3 (force-us-east-f32), bench-178980-4 (force-eu-west-int8)
Ryan: results (quick):
```
bench-178980-1 (nearest): p50 58ms p95 100ms
bench-178980-2 (cost-priority): p50 85ms p95 370ms
bench-178980-3 (force us-east f32): p50 82ms p95 330ms
bench-178980-4 (force eu-west int8): p50 56ms p95 98ms
```
Lei: that strongly implicates routing -> cross-pop kernel mismatch. int8 on eu-west much faster tail.
Maya: root cause clear. mitigation options: revert policy for v2-quant, or ensure consistent kernel profiles across regions, or add an affinity rule to prefer same-kernel replicas. thoughts?
Devon: short-term: revert the cost-priority rule for that tag. mid-term: add kernel-profile label to routing decision and autosync kernel builds.
Sasha: we should also add a perf check to rollout pipeline: if cloud-region p95 increases >25% after routing update, auto-rollback.
Ryan: i'll open a PR for a routing rollback and a follow-up ops-runbook for kernel-sync.
Maya: thanks. @PerfBot can you post a dashboard link and attach the bench artifacts to the ticket?
PerfBot: done: https://rwd.internal/perf/bench-178980 artifacts attached to ticket RI-5821
Devon: filed rollback RFC: https://rwd.internal/ops/rollbacks/RI-5821-RB
Maya: nice. let's loop back after rollback and kernel sync. :thumbsup:
